correctness.rationale: In a finite local ring, unit status is precisely nonzero residue; hence distinct vertices are adjacent iff their two residues do not sum to zero. This yields the balanced complete multipartite graph in residue characteristic two and a complement consisting of K_s plus (q−1)/2 copies of K_(s,s) in odd characteristic. Each residue fiber consists of twins. Three white fibers leave every blue vertex with at least two white neighbors; two distinct white fibers allow a blue vertex in a fiber that misses one residue to force the other white. When the required source is in one of the white fibers a blue vertex is available since s>=2. The graph has no isolates, so one remaining white can always be forced. This gives the polynomial, all minimizers, and the exact inversion from N and c. The rank-two witnesses fit the odd regime and K_(s,s). In the remaining regime nilpotence gives m/m² nonzero, thus s>=q>=4. Rank two cannot accommodate three or more parts of size at least three: each part must use a distinct isotropic line in a nondegenerate real bilinear plane. The squared-difference matrix of distinct real labels, repeated within each part, has rank at most three and the exact pattern. Thus M=N−mr gives the claimed transition. Independent replay python /workspace/audit_checks.py 2 exhausts every initial subset for Z/4, Z/8, Z/9 and the F4 dual numbers and tests each coloring against the profile rule; the 16-vertex case gives {14:96,15:16,16:1}. Finite corroboration is separate from the rank and forcing proofs. The recognition statement is relative to the stated graph class, not ring reconstruction.

originality.rationale: The entire finding is covered by direct specialization and elementary inversion. Boyer et al. Proposition 4 directly gives the even polynomial and profiles. For the odd branch, Barrett–van der Holst–Loewy equation (4.1) and Corollary 2 give mr<=2 on exactly this complement shape (and mr>=2 since it is connected and noncomplete). Thus M=N−2 and no forcing set is smaller. Boyer et al. Theorem 1(1)–(3), not merely its multipartite proposition, gives the complete polynomial on that branch: its n−2 pairs are precisely nontwin pairs of nonisolates, here all pairs from different fibers. Distinct residues have distinct missing-neighbor fibers and s>=2 gives a witness outside the two vertices. The remaining real rank values follow from K_(s,s) and the induced K_(3,3,3) obstruction (Barrett et al. Observation 6(b)) plus the classical rank <=3 univariate squared-distance matrix, using one coordinate per part. This is exactly the frozen upper witness, expressed in distance notation. M=N−mr then gives the transition. Solving the resulting known coefficient identity for q and s, which already specify the graph, is mechanical rather than a distinct theorem at the claimed level. The decision rests on these verified implications, not on unavailable literature or on an exact-title match.
